objective: By the end of the lesson, learners will be better able to use coordinating conjunctions (and, but, or, so) to write compound sentences in the context of describing a memorable event.
materials:
- Coursebook: Introduction to Academic Writing, Chapter 2, pp 30-32
- Grammar accuracy feedback: 31-05-26-M3-3A-combined.pdf

stages.stage_aim: To activate awareness of their own writing errors and build motivation for the grammar focus
stages.procedure: - Distribute individual grammar accuracy feedback from the ERRANT PDF. Ss review their errors silently (3 min). Highlight class patterns: comma splices are the most common error. 'Your next CA is a narrative paragraph about a memorable event. But first — how do we join two sentences correctly?' Write goal on board.

stages.stage_aim: To diagnose baseline ability to combine simple sentences into compound sentences
stages.procedure: - Display 6 pairs of simple sentences on screen. Ss join each pair into one compound using and/but/or/so. No instruction given — pure discovery task. Individual (4 min). Pair check (2 min). Teacher circulates, notes common errors in coordinator choice and comma placement.

stages.stage: Teach — Coordinators: and, but, or, so
stages.stage_aim: To clarify the meaning and function of the four coordinating conjunctions in compound sentences
stages.procedure: - Display compound sentence formula: SV, and SV. Elicit: 'What makes a sentence compound?' (two subjects, two verb groups, comma + coordinator). Walk through each coordinator's meaning using textbook examples from the folktale on p.29. Highlight comma rule: comma BEFORE coordinator.

stages.stage_aim: To give structured practice identifying coordinating conjunctions and classifying simple vs compound sentences
stages.procedure: - Ss complete Practice 2A: circle coordinating conjunctions in the folktale 'Omusubi Kororin' and explain why some have commas (5 min). Then Practice 2B: label CS or SS for items 1-10, add commas (7 min). Pair check (3 min). Whole-class feedback on screen.

stages.stage_aim: To give extended practice choosing coordinators and writing original compound sentences
stages.procedure: - Practice 2C: Ss combine 8 sentence pairs using and/but/or/so (6 min). Pair compare (2 min). Display model answers. Then Practice 2D: Ss write 5 original compound sentences following the directions on p.32 (p. 36 if using new edition). Begin in class, finish for homework if needed.

stages.stage_aim: To consolidate key learning and connect to the narrative paragraph CA task
stages.procedure: - Quick review: 'How do you make a compound sentence?' (SV, coordinator SV). 'What does but signal?' (contrast). 'Where does the comma go?' (before coordinator). Connect to CA: 'In your paragraph about a memorable event, use compound sentences.' Preview: 'Next lesson — comma rules and freewriting.'
